title: Short Stuff: Vantablack
summary: Short Stuff episode on Vantablack, the ultra-black material made from vertically aligned carbon nanotubes by Surrey NanoSystems. The hosts cover why it absorbs nearly all visible light (about 99.965 percent), its original purpose for space and optical applications, and its use by BMW for an X6 car study and by H. Moser and Company in a $75,000 watch. They discuss the MIT blacker-than-Vantablack material from 2019, artist Stuart Semple's competing blacks and his feud with artist Anish Kapoor, who holds the exclusive license to Vantablack, and Kapoor's Vantablack-lined eggs at the Hirshhorn Museum in D.C. The episode also includes a Spinal Tap "none more black" tangent.

segments.title: Opening and why Vantablack is interesting
segments.summary: Josh introduces the topic, recalling choosing a black paint for his office, and notes Vantablack's expense and the license held by Anish Kapoor.

segments.title: How Vantablack works
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Vantablack is made of vertically aligned carbon nanotubes, very tall and tightly packed, which trap light and convert it to heat, leaving little reflection and a silhouette-only look. Surrey NanoSystems is named as the maker.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break before the discussion continues.

segments.title: Spinal Tap none more black joke
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss the Spinal Tap 'none more black' album joke as an aside.

segments.title: Uses: space, optics, art and design
segments.summary: The original purpose was space travel and improving visibility in telescopes by absorbing stray light. Artists and designers were drawn to it, and BMW used a version to paint an X6 to study its silhouette, reportedly as a publicity stunt. A version was not the original material; BMW needed different nanotube arrangements suitable for car paint.

segments.title: H. Moser watch and MIT blacker black
segments.summary: H. Moser and Company released a $75,000 Vantablack watch face. The hosts report that a 2019 MIT group created a blacker material using carbon nanotubes that absorbs 99.5 percent of visible light, and that Vantablack absorbs 99.965 percent.

segments.title: Artist coatings and Stuart Semple
segments.summary: Artist Stuart Semple sells blacker paints (Black 2.0 and Black 3.0) and his own pigments, and the hosts describe a sales restriction requiring buyers to affirm they are not Anish Kapoor or associated with him. A German artist, named by the hosts as Streibe, coated a diamond with the new black.

segments.title: Kapoor feud and Hirshhorn eggs
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Semple versus Kapoor art feud over the Vantablack license and mention Kapoor's giant eggs lined with Vantablack at the Hirshhorn Museum in D.C.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and joke about a future Short Stuff on the feud.
